newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND'S CORKERY MAY MISS ENGLISH GAME.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-IRELAND'S CORKERY MAY MISS ENGLISH GAME.

text.p: Ireland blind-side flanker David Corkery said on Tuesday a finger injury might force him to miss the Five Nations championship meeting with England at Lansdowne Road on February 15.

Corkery, 24, damaged the third finger on his right hand when making a tackle in the 26-25 defeat of Wales in Cardiff on Saturday and was due to see a surgeon in Bristol on Tuesday to assess the extent of the injury.

"I pushed it (the finger) back in place and played on but I don't know what the situation is now. I'll have to wait for the medical reports and I will then be in contact with the Irish team management," Corkery said.
"It would be a terrible blow to miss the English match because it is the one I am looking forward to but it is not looking good at the moment. But who knows? Maybe it is not as bad first appears."
On a more encouraging note for Ireland, winger Simon Geoghegan is expected to make a return for Bath's second team next weekend after a long lay-off with a toe injury.
